ref: DAR — Revelation ch. 4: A New Vision: The Heavenly Sanctuary
title: A New Vision: The Heavenly Sanctuary
voicePrompt: Explain in your own words why Smith argues that the apartment John saw opened is the heavenly sanctuary, and describe what John sees there — the throne, the twenty-four elders, the seven lamps, the sea of glass, and the four living creatures.

questions.stem: According to Smith, what does the phrase "after this" in verse 1 indicate?
options: That the events of chapter 4 onward occur only after everything in chapters 1-3 is fulfilled
That after seeing and hearing what was recorded in the first three chapters, John had the new view he now introduces
That the first three chapters are out of chronological order
That John fell asleep between the two visions
questions.explanation: Smith states that "after this" does not mean chapter 4 onward takes place after everything in the preceding chapters is fulfilled, but only that after John had seen and heard what is recorded there, he had the new view he now introduces.

questions.stem: Why does Smith emphasize that John says a door was opened "in heaven" rather than "into heaven"?
options: Because heaven itself was opened before John's mind, as it was for Stephen
Because the door represents Christ as the way of access
Because a place or apartment in heaven was opened so John could behold what was transpiring within
Because John was still standing on earth and looking upward
questions.explanation: Smith contrasts this with Stephen's experience: it was not an opening of heaven itself before John's mind, but some place or apartment in heaven was opened before him so he could behold what was transpiring within — and this apartment was the heavenly sanctuary.

questions.stem: How does Smith identify the twenty-four elders?
options: As the twelve patriarchs and twelve apostles representing all Israel
As angels who have never been part of the human race
As redeemed persons from earth, among those raised at Christ's resurrection and led up on high when He ascended
As symbolic figures with no real-world counterpart
questions.explanation: Smith argues the elders are redeemed persons, redeemed by Christ's blood from this earth, identified with the saints who arose at Christ's resurrection (Matthew 27:52-53) and the "multitude of captives" He led up when He ascended (Ephesians 4:8).

questions.stem: What does Smith say the seven lamps of fire are an antitype of, and what does their presence prove?
options: The seven branches of the menorah, proving John saw the temple in Jerusalem
The golden candlestick of the typical sanctuary, proving John is looking into the first apartment of the sanctuary above
The seven churches of Asia, proving the vision is about the church age
The seven days of creation, proving God's authority as Creator
questions.explanation: Smith says the seven lamps of fire are an antitype of the golden candlestick of the typical sanctuary, which was placed in the first apartment of the earthly sanctuary; seeing this antitype is good proof John is looking into the first apartment of the sanctuary above.

questions.stem: How does Smith treat the word "beasts" used for the four living creatures in verse 6?
options: He defends it as the most accurate rendering of the Greek
He calls it a very unhappy translation, noting the Greek word means a living creature and differs from the word for the prophetic beasts
He says it proves the creatures are wild animals symbolizing earthly kingdoms
He treats it as identical to the beast of chapter 13
questions.explanation: Smith calls it "a very unhappy translation," explaining the Greek word denotes a living creature and is very different from the word used for the prophetic beasts of chapter 13 and following.

questions.stem: According to Smith, what qualities do the emblems of the four living creatures (lion, calf, man, eagle) signify?
options: Power, wealth, wisdom, and beauty
The four Gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John
Strength, perseverance, reason, and swiftness
Justice, mercy, truth, and peace
questions.explanation: Smith says the qualities signified are strength, perseverance, reason, and swiftness — strength of affection, perseverance in carrying out duty, reason in comprehending the divine will, and swiftness in obeying.

questions.stem: Why, according to Smith, do the living creatures never grow weary of repeating "Holy, holy, holy"?
options: Because they are commanded to do so without ceasing as a penalty
Because with every utterance they gain a new view of God's attributes, so the words never grow old to them
Because they are unable to speak any other words
Because the repetition keeps them awake through the heavenly night
questions.explanation: Smith explains that praise does not become monotonous to them because with every utterance they gain a new view of God's attributes; the horizon expands, their hearts enlarge, and the words never grow old.

questions.stem: What does Smith say furnishes the foundation for the honor, glory, and power ascribed to God in verse 11?
options: The redemption of the elders and living creatures
The covenant symbolized by the rainbow around the throne
The works of creation, since God willed and all things came into existence
The judgment scene described in Daniel 7
questions.explanation: Smith states that the works of creation furnish the foundation for the honor, glory, and power ascribed to God: God willed, and all things came into existence, and by the same power they are preserved and sustained.
